title: The future of security
syllabusUnit: Unit V: Post-Quantum Cryptography & Modern Primitives
covers: Post-quantum (Kyber/Dilithium), zero-knowledge intuition, blockchain hashing & Merkle, passkeys/WebAuthn
learningGoals: You will be able to explain how quantum computers (Shor's algorithm) threaten RSA and ECC.
You will be able to illustrate Zero-Knowledge Proofs using the Ali Baba Cave analogy.
You will be able to describe how FIDO2 / WebAuthn passkeys replace passwords with public keys.

lessonCards.title: The Quantum Threat: Shor vs Grover
lessonCards.analogy: A quantum super-key that unlocks all classical factoring padlocks in seconds.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Peter Shor proved in 1994 that quantum computers running Shor's algorithm can factor integers and solve discrete logarithms in polynomial time, breaking RSA, DH, and ECC.
lessonCards.example: Grover's algorithm halves symmetric security (AES-128 becomes 64-bit strength, but AES-256 remains safe at 128-bit quantum strength).

lessonCards.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC)
lessonCards.analogy: Building locks out of high-dimensional multi-directional crystal lattices instead of simple numbers.
lessonCards.coreConcept: NIST standardized lattice-based post-quantum algorithms in 2024: ML-KEM (Kyber) for key encapsulation and ML-DSA (Dilithium) for digital signatures.
lessonCards.example: Lattice problems remain computationally intractable for both classical and quantum computers.

lessonCards.title: Zero-Knowledge & Passkeys (WebAuthn)
lessonCards.analogy: Proving you know the secret cave password by walking in one entrance and emerging from the other without ever saying the word.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) mathematically prove a statement is true without revealing any secret data. FIDO2 / WebAuthn replaces passwords with hardware-backed public keys.
lessonCards.example: Passkeys use device TouchID/FaceID to sign challenges, making phishing completely impossible.

questions.prompt: What impact will large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers running Shor's algorithm have on modern classical cryptography?
options: They will completely break RSA, Diffie-Hellman, and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) in polynomial time
They will break symmetric AES-256 completely
They will have zero impact on security
They will make the internet 100x slower
questions.explanation: Shor's algorithm solves both prime factorization and the discrete logarithm problem in polynomial time O(n^3), dismantling classical public-key cryptography.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Shor's algorithm renders RSA and ECC insecure.
Grover's algorithm only halves symmetric key space; AES-256 retains 128 bits of security.
The impact is profound and requires global migration to PQC.
Quantum processing does not affect optical network transit speed.
questions.realWorldExample: NIST initiated the Post-Quantum Cryptography standardization project in 2016 to replace RSA and ECC.

questions.prompt: Which mathematical structure forms the foundation of the newly standardized NIST Post-Quantum algorithms ML-KEM (Kyber) and ML-DSA (Dilithium)?
options: High-dimensional Lattice-based cryptography (Learning With Errors / LWE)
Basic clock arithmetic
Monoalphabetic substitution
Simple binary XOR
questions.explanation: Lattice-based cryptography relies on the hardness of finding the shortest vector in high-dimensional geometric grids, which quantum computers cannot solve efficiently.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Module-Lattice cryptography provides post-quantum security.
Modular clock math is broken by Shor's algorithm.
Substitution is trivial classical crypto.
XOR alone is symmetric.
questions.realWorldExample: FIPS 203 (ML-KEM) and FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) were finalized by NIST in August 2024.

questions.prompt: In the famous 'Ali Baba Cave' parable, what does the story illustrate about Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)?
options: Peggy proves to Victor that she knows the secret magic word to open the door without ever speaking the word to Victor
Ali Baba finds stolen gold in an open desert
A password is sent in clear HTTP text
A computer encrypts files with a key
questions.explanation: By repeatedly entering the circular cave through path A or B and emerging from whichever path Victor shouts, Peggy proves she can unlock the door without revealing the secret word.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Zero-Knowledge Proofs confirm truth without leaking private data.
Folktales are analogies.
ZKPs prevent cleartext transmission.
Encryption is distinct from zero-knowledge verification.
questions.realWorldExample: ZK-SNARKs enable private cryptocurrency transactions and privacy-preserving identity verification.

questions.prompt: What makes FIDO2 / WebAuthn 'Passkeys' completely immune to credential phishing attacks?
options: Passkeys bind public-key signatures directly to the browser's verified website origin domain
Passkeys require typing a 100-character master key
Passkeys are written on paper cards
Passkeys turn off website links
questions.explanation: The browser validates the cryptographic domain origin; if you visit a fake lookalike phishing site, your hardware key will refuse to sign the challenge.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Domain binding eliminates phishing because keys never respond to spoofed domains.
Users authenticate with biometrics (FaceID/fingerprint) without typing passwords.
Passkeys reside in hardware secure enclaves.
Links remain clickable.
questions.realWorldExample: Apple, Google, and Microsoft have deployed passkeys as the passwordless successor to legacy logins.

questions.prompt: What is a 'Merkle Tree' and where is it fundamentally used in modern computing?
options: A hierarchical tree of cryptographic hashes where every parent node is the hash of its children, enabling efficient tamper-proof verification
A tree planted in computer server rooms
A sorting algorithm used in databases
A tree of symmetric AES keys
questions.explanation: Ralph Merkle patented Merkle trees in 1979; they allow verifying whether a specific transaction exists in a huge block with only O(log n) hash proofs.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Merkle trees enable cryptographic verification of huge datasets in Git, Bitcoin, and Certificate Transparency.
Trees are metaphorical data structures.
Sorting is an algorithm.
AES keys are symmetric strings.
questions.realWorldExample: Git commit integrity and Bitcoin block headers rely directly on Merkle trees.

questions.prompt: What is the 'Store Now, Decrypt Later' (SNDL) threat posed by hostile state adversaries today?
options: Adversaries intercept and record encrypted government and health data today, planning to decrypt it once quantum computers arrive
Adversaries destroy cloud data centers
Adversaries sell hard drives on eBay
Adversaries wait until night to hack computers
questions.explanation: Adversaries intercept encrypted military and financial traffic now, banking on the certainty that quantum hardware in 10-15 years will factor the keys.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Data with long shelf-lives (20-30 years) must migrate to post-quantum encryption immediately.
SNDL is passive harvesting, not physical destruction.
Hardware auctions are unrelated.
Harvesting occurs 24/7 across internet backbones.
questions.realWorldExample: This threat is why NSA and NIST are urgently accelerating the transition to PQC standards today.

ashRecap: The future of security is already here! Lattice crystals protect against quantum computers, Zero-Knowledge proves truth without revealing secrets, and Passkeys kill phishing forever!
